review_notes: I read the whole file. The helper sections T2Aux and TCAux are where the simp-interface issues are. I treated the very long `solution` theorem as a proof-only section with no simp interface and found no simp-specific problems in it. I read `Place.evalAt_one`, `evalAt_of_mem`, `evalAt_mul_of_mem` and `evalAt_algebraMap_eq` in the Definitions files to check which simp lemmas already exist. I did not check whether adding `@[simp]` to the lemmas below would break other files that import this one. The `attribute [-simp]` lines list many names, and I did not exhaustively check them against these findings. All proposals are untested, since I cannot run Lean.

findings.excerpt:
theorem evalAt_algebraMap (P : Place K F) (hP : P.IsRational) (a : K) :
    P.evalAt (algebraMap K F a) = a := by
findings.problem: The identity `P.evalAt (algebraMap K F a) = a` is the canonical normal form for evaluating a constant. It has no `@[simp]` attribute here. The library already has the same statement as `Place.evalAt_algebraMap_eq` (also without `@[simp]`), and that version assumes no rationality hypothesis. This local copy needs `hP : P.IsRational` and a longer proof. Because neither version is simp, constants under `evalAt` are rewritten by hand, as in `rw [evalAt_algebraMap P hP]` at line 168.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the local `evalAt_algebraMap` and use `Place.evalAt_algebraMap_eq`, which takes no rationality hypothesis. Make that library lemma `@[simp]`. Its left side `v.evalAt (algebraMap K F a)` is a fixed shape and its right side is a strictly smaller term, so a rewrite loop is not credible. If the library lemma cannot be changed, mark the local copy `@[simp]` instead.
findings.benefit: `simp` can then reduce `evalAt (algebraMap K F a)` to `a` automatically. It also removes the duplicate lemma and the unnecessary `hP` argument.

findings.declaration: T2Aux.compVal (zero_mem' field) and the evalAt_mul/add/neg/sub family
findings.excerpt:
have : P.evalAt (0 : F) = 0 := by
      rw [← ev_eq_evalAt P hP 0 (zero_mem _)]
findings.problem: The library has `@[simp] Place.evalAt_one`, but the matching `evalAt 0 = 0` fact is proved inline inside `zero_mem'`. It is never stated as a named lemma. Lines 147 and 162 then use `exact zero_mem _` after a manual rewrite. The sibling lemmas `evalAt_mul`, `evalAt_add`, `evalAt_neg`, `evalAt_sub` (lines 101–115) are also proved here with side conditions `hf : f ∈ P.toValuationSubring`. They are used only through explicit `rw [evalAt_… P hP hf hg]`. This makes the interface for `evalAt` asymmetric: `evalAt 1` is simp, while `evalAt 0` and the ring operations are not.
findings.proposed_change: State `theorem evalAt_zero (P : Place K F) : P.evalAt (0 : F) = 0` and mark it `@[simp]`. It needs no rationality hypothesis, because `evalAt_of_mem` gives `residueInv (residue 0)`, and `residueInv` of an `algebraMap` image is injective-inverse. Use it in `zero_mem'`. For `evalAt_mul/add/neg/sub`, keep the side-condition form and consider marking them `@[simp]` with the membership hypotheses as discharger goals. Alternatively, state an `evalAt` ring hom on the valuation subring (the existing `ev`) and register simp lemmas for that.
findings.benefit: This gives one canonical simp normal form for `evalAt` on constants and removes the inline proof. It also avoids the repeated `rw [… evalAt_mul …, Place.evalAt_one]` sequences, such as those at lines 153 and 183.

findings.excerpt:
theorem mem_compVal_iff {f : F} : f ∈ compVal P hP A ↔ f ∈ P.toValuationSubring ∧ P.evalAt f ∈ A :=
  ⟨fun h => h, fun h => h⟩
findings.problem: This is the membership-unfolding lemma for the new `compVal` definition. Its proof is `Iff.rfl` in disguise, and it is not `@[simp]`. Downstream code never uses it. It instead reaches into membership proofs with projections, for example `hf.2` and `hf.1` in `isUnit_compVal_iff` (lines 171–190). Constructions such as `⟨f⁻¹, hfiP, hfiA⟩` and `⟨P.algebraMap_mem' a, …⟩` rely on definitional unfolding. `simp` therefore cannot turn `f ∈ compVal P hP A` into its two conjuncts.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `mem_compVal_iff` as `@[simp]`, since its left side is headed by the specific constant `compVal`. Optionally add `Iff.rfl` as the proof. Then state `isUnit_compVal_iff`, `coe_mem_nonunits_compVal_iff` and `algebraMap_mem_compVal` using `simp [mem_compVal_iff]` instead of `.1`/`.2` projections.
findings.benefit: This gives the standard unfolding simp lemma for a bespoke carrier set. Membership goals such as `f ∈ compVal P hP A` reduce to the two data conditions without relying on definitional unfolding, and proofs stay robust if the structure of `compVal` changes.
